cases.statement: One carrier: P5 (the index case) of PMID 37324276, a 39-year-old man with type 1 diabetes from age 19, oral and genital ulcers since early childhood, raised liver enzymes and thyroid autoantibodies; heterozygous; parents and sister negative. The review 39125844 (Table 2 row 36) summarises the same man, citing PMID 37324276 as [56].

people.label: P5
people.key_phenotypes: type 1 diabetes from age 19 (anti-GAD positive, no ketoacidosis); recurrent oral and genital ulcers since early childhood; elevated liver transaminases; thyroid autoantibodies (Hashimoto thyroiditis in Table 2); arthralgia (Table 2)

quotes.quote: A 39-year-old male patient with hyperglycemia for 20 years was admitted to the Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University.
He was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus at the age of 19 years and has been on insulin therapy since then.
He also had recurring and minor oral and genital ulcers since early childhood.

As shown in Table 1, laboratory examination results revealed reduced islet function, a normal lipid profile, an HbA1c of 7%, increased glutamate decarboxylase (GAD) antibodies, elevated liver transaminases, and increased thyroid-related antibodies with normal thyroid function.

Gln490Ter (c.1467_1468delinsAT) was found in a patient who had liver dysfunctions and minor mouth ulcers since early childhood, and he was diagnosed with Type-1 diabetes at the age of 19.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Testing was prompted by atypical features for type 1 diabetes (adolescent diagnosis without ketoacidosis, preserved islet function, unexplained liver abnormality, early Behçet-like ulcers). The authors state other liver diseases were excluded but name no tests. Whole-exome sequencing was done; the paper does not state whether the known monogenic autoimmune-diabetes genes it lists were specifically excluded.

quotes.quote: The patient was diagnosed in adolescence and never had ketoacidosis, his islet function was still not completely failed after such a long time (fasting C-peptide: >200 pmol/L), his abnormal liver function could not be reasonably explained, and he had early onset Behcet’s-like disease symptom.
In this case, liver function revealed abnormally elevated transaminases, excluding other liver diseases.

Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome high-throughput sequencing technology, and the data were analyzed using the Verita Trekker® Variant Site Detection System and Enliven® Variant Site Annotation Interpretation System developed by Berry Genetics.
To date, nine disease-causing genes have been reported, including AIRE, CTLA4, FOXP3, IL2RA, ITCH, LRBA, SIRT1, STAT1, and STAT3 (1–3).

segregation.statement: Parents (healthy, nonconsanguineous) and sister tested and lack the variant. No other affected relatives reported; the patient has no children.

quotes.quote: The patient’s parents and sister were found to be devoid of this variant.
His parents are healthy and nonconsanguineous.
He is a married man with no children.

de_novo.statement: Both parents tested and lack the variant (the paper does not use the words 'de novo'). Parentage confirmation is not reported.

quotes.quote: The patient’s parents and sister were found to be devoid of this variant.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-nucleotide substitution (delins) creating a stop codon, p.(Gln490Ter) per the batch HGVS (agrees with the paper's p.Q490*), in zinc finger 2 per the paper. The paper describes HA20 as caused by loss-of-function variants with insufficient A20 production.

quotes.quote: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a monogenic autosomal-dominant genetic autoinflammatory disease caused by loss of function mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene.
HA20 is an autosomal-dominant genetic disease in which the NF-kB signaling pathway is less inhibited because of insufficient A20 production.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a novel pathogenic mutation. No ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: In conclusion, we report a novel pathogenic mutation in TNFAIP3 that results in HA20 in a T1DM patient.

concerns: The paper contradicts itself on the protein: the text and Table 2 give p.Q490*, while the Figure 1 legend gives 'p.Glu490*'. The batch protein p.(Gln490Ter) agrees with the text.
The paper contradicts itself on arthralgia: Table 2 marks arthralgia 'yes' for P5 (this patient), but the discussion says the five T1DM patients did not have arthralgia or arthritis.

Onset is reported differently: ulcers 'since early childhood' in the text, initial symptoms at age 5 in Table 2, and onset '19 years' (age at diabetes) in the review 39125844. The abstract says 'minor mouth ulcers', while the case report says oral and genital ulcers.
39125844 (review) is a secondary summary of the same man, not an independent case.
Transcript not stated; the batch uses NM_001270508.2. The paper places the variant in exon 7.
notes_for_panel: A single proband with both parents tested negative; parentage not confirmed. Phenotype is type 1 diabetes plus Behçet-like ulcers and liver involvement. No functional data.
